sensitive_conditions: Fresh samples and arbitrary persistent reuse are different oracle permissions.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Per-instance success >=2/3. Upper has deterministic separate caps on every path. Lower covers worst-case deterministic caps and worst-case expected total budgets separately.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: May depend on fixed scale bounds; tildes hide logarithms in dimension and inverse tolerances, never polynomial dimension dependence.
complexity_scope.oracle: Upper uses separate complete gradients/Hessians. Lower also holds for a stronger unit-cost sampled value-gradient-complete-Hessian bundle with retained handles.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Point satisfying both gradient norm <=epsilon and minimum Hessian eigenvalue >=-gamma; failure symbol counts as failure.
complexity_scope.regime: Fixed positive scales, sufficiently small independent tolerances, every finite d for upper and d>=d_star for lower.
complexity_scope.resource: Total derivative evaluations N_g+N_H in Definition 2; same-sample endpoints and separate derivatives charged separately. Stronger bundled lower oracle charges one per bundle.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Upper: Algorithm 1 with separate derivative trees. Lower: all measurable adaptive randomized algorithms with arbitrary persistent reuse, unrestricted queries and unqueried outputs.

map: Import the upper witness from the batch's explicit-upper-budget theorem, preserving its separate mixed terms and all-path caps.

Curvature interface, Section 6.1: the smooth gate chain q_n uses n=Theta(gamma^-3), a random orthonormal frame, scaling h=K gamma and a bounded-gradient radial wall with radius R=K_R/gamma. Lemmas 3–4 provide exact order-two-jet truncation and exclusion of incomplete/exterior successful outputs. Conditional spherical tails couple the ideal sequential-revelation transcript to the actual full-jet oracle, including the final unqueried output. Required dimension is O(gamma^-4 log(1/gamma)+gamma^-3).

First-order interface, Section 6.2: independent hidden sign blocks, alpha=D^(1/4), q_j=(2/D)sum_l theta_jl tanh(alpha x_jl), flat gates and a conservative scalar chain plus log-cosh regularizer force every stationary output to activate every block. Each handle retains an independently sampled coefficient table Z_jl in {-R,R}, with mean theta_jl and R=c_R s_star/epsilon. Equations (6.16)–(6.20), using third-order localization, realize one scalar sample loss with the required common sample Hessian-Lipschitz bound.

Persistent information interface: a stronger response reveals a relevant handle–block array on first use. Its KL relative to a fair array is <=C D/R^2; repeat uses of the same revealed array have zero additional conditional KL. Lemma 7 bounds stagewise progress, includes far activation and final output, and charges at most one historical stage per response. Theorem 6.1 yields Omega(Delta s_star^2/(epsilon^3 D^(1/4))) in dimension O(Delta D^(3/4)/epsilon).

Section 6.3 pads either hard family with unused coordinates into common dimension max{d_epsilon,d_gamma}; responses in added coordinates reveal nothing and successful outputs project to successful original outputs. Taking the larger endpoint lower bound gives Theorem 4.2. Truncation arguments at the component endpoints also give worst-case expected-cost lower bounds.
Corollary 1 combines the two endpoint lower bounds and the upper bound; D_epsilon is logarithmic for fixed scales and max{a,b}>=(a+b)/2. No new cross-paper transfer is claimed.

assumptions: Fix positive Delta,L1,L2,sigma_g,sigma_H,G. The objective is bounded below and f(x0)-inf f<=Delta at the specified initial point.
On a common probability-one set F(.;xi) is C^2 and, for all x,y, its gradient is L1-Lipschitz and Hessian L2-Lipschitz.
The population f is C^2 and expectations commute with derivatives through order two.
On a common probability-one set, for every x, ||grad F-grad f||<=sigma_g and ||Hess F-Hess f||<=sigma_H. Also sup_x||grad f(x)||<=G.
Algorithms may revisit any saved sample arbitrarily often and select unrestricted query locations and unqueried outputs.
statement.conclusion: Theorem 4.2 requires worst-case total budget at least c max{Delta s_star^2/(epsilon^3 D_epsilon^(1/4)),gamma^-3} for d>=d_star. This remains necessary with worst-case expected total cost and when a unit-cost call returns the sampled value, complete gradient and complete Hessian jointly. Theorem 4.1 attains N_g=tilde-O(epsilon^-3+epsilon^-2 gamma^-1), N_H=tilde-O(epsilon^-2+epsilon^-1 gamma^-2+gamma^-3) under separate all-path caps. Corollary 1 therefore states Q_tot^star(epsilon,gamma)=tilde-Theta(epsilon^-3+gamma^-3) in the growing-dimension convention. The attainable pair does not characterize the full (N_g,N_H) Pareto frontier.
statement.objects_and_definitions: On R^d use Euclidean and induced operator norms. A measurable scalar sample loss F has finite population expectation f=E F. An (epsilon,gamma)-SOSP has ||grad f||<=epsilon and lambda_min(Hess f)>=-gamma. Opaque handles independently sample F once and retain that sample forever. Requesting a handle supplies no observation and is free. One gradient or one complete Hessian costs one evaluation; both cost two; a same-sample endpoint difference costs two. Computation is free. Queries and outputs are arbitrary measurable functions of history and private randomness; output need not have been queried. Bottom is failure. Q_d^star is the least deterministic total cap achieving success >=2/3 on every admissible d-dimensional instance. Q_tot^star summarizes finite-d upper bounds and sufficiently-large-d lower bounds as specified in Section 3.1.
statement.parameter_domains: Let s_star=min{1,sigma_g,sigma_H,L1,L2,G} and D_epsilon=ceil(C log(2+Delta/epsilon+Delta s_star^2/epsilon^3)), with sufficiently large numerical C. For sufficiently small independent positive tolerances, d_star<=C_d(1+Delta D_epsilon^(3/4)/epsilon+gamma^-4 log(2/gamma)+gamma^-3). Constants c,C_d may depend on the fixed scale bounds, not tolerances. The upper witness allows 0<epsilon,gamma<=1 and every finite d>=1.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: Fix the six positive scale bounds before taking sufficiently small independent epsilon,gamma>0. There is a dimension threshold d_star such that for every d>=d_star, every adaptive randomized algorithm succeeding with probability >=2/3 on every admissible instance has the stated worst-case total budget lower bound. A hard fixed instance may depend on the algorithm. The same order is necessary for worst-case expected budgets and for the stronger joint oracle. The upper witness succeeds on every instance and every finite dimension, with private signs and independent sampled losses.
